results.summary: Valproate is contraindicated or should be used with extreme caution in hepatic impairment — causes dose-dependent hyperammonemia via urea cycle inhibition and is hepatotoxic. Lamotrigine requires slow titration to avoid Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

Lamotrigine has a renal elimination pathway and lacks known hepatotoxic effects in the published literature.

key_clinical_evidence: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Valproate can produce hyperammonemic encephalopathy in patients without overt liver disease (urea-cycle inhibition); in cirrhotics the effect is potentiated. L-carnitine reverses it.
Thiazides reduce lithium clearance; the lithium-HCTZ combination is a well-known cause of toxicity.
